From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.
7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as
a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.
8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each
(AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether
each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale
consent is required merely because shares are sold.
10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of
the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the
Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Seller's update note and Disclosure Letter only. I have not seen the full SPA mark-up or the underlying data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012). Clause references are the Seller's, and points flagged "verify" need checking against the source documents.

---

## 1. Overall assessment

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced". Taken together, it would leave the Buyer with almost no effective protection. The key reasons:

- **Protection is hollowed out from both ends.** General disclosure of the whole data room, plus a "discoverable" knowledge bar (cl 8.3), means almost any claim can be defeated. Meanwhile the caps, time limits and exclusive-remedy provisions are extended to *all* Claims, including title, tax and indemnities.
- **Known, quantifiable problems are pushed onto the warranty regime.** Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the DD-006 incident, the DD-005 bonuses and the Sandbar renewals are all identified, live risks. Because they are disclosed, warranties will not respond to them, and W&I insurance would exclude them as known matters. They need specific indemnities, conditions, completion deliverables or price adjustments.
- **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its update note.** Section 2 states there is no final Bluefen consent or evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. Section 3 states Riverlark is unpaid and undischarged. Section 4 states there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment for Ironquay. Section 5 states the bonuses are omitted from the funds flow. Section 6 states the incident investigation is preliminary. Section 11 states no conclusions are drawn. The update note's reassurances ("addressed", "adequate", "not expected to be material", "ordinary course", "settled") are not supported by the Seller's own disclosure.
- **The disclosure is stale.** It speaks as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. We should require an updated disclosure position and a bring-down at signing and Completion.

---

## 2. Material issues and pushback

### Tier 1: Deal-critical (structure, title, value leakage)

**2.1 Riverlark facility, about AUD 3.2m (cl 2/7)**
- *Seller position:* release to be provided after Completion.
- *Problem:* This is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis. DD-003 contains a change-control clause (8.1), so Completion itself may trigger a default or acceleration while the security remains over the Company's assets. A post-Completion release is a bare promise from a Seller who will by then have been paid.
- *Push for:*
  - Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price, as a line item in the funds flow, paid directly to Riverlark.
  - Completion deliverables: a signed payout letter stating the exact payoff amount (including break costs and interest to Completion), a deed of release, and PPSR financing change statements (or an undertaking from Riverlark to register them within a short period).
  - All Riverlark amounts treated as Debt reducing the equity price.
  - A waiver of cl 8.1, or confirmation it is not triggered, as a condition to Completion if repayment cannot be locked in.

**2.2 Title (DD-012)**
- *Seller position:* title is evidenced by the Company's own share register, and title and capacity warranties are subject to the general cap and time limits.
- *Problem:* A self-maintained register is not sufficient evidence of title. Capping title at 20% of price and 18 months is not acceptable for a 100% share acquisition. The Seller's own §10 concedes the Buyer has not verified title.
- *Push for:*
  - Title and capacity treated as **Fundamental Warranties**, capped at 100% of the price and claimable for at least 6 years. NSW limitation periods are 6 years for simple contracts and 12 years for deeds, so consider executing the SPA as a deed.
  - Excluded from the de minimis, basket, general disclosure and knowledge bar.
  - Our own verification: ASIC company extract and historical share issue/transfer filings, share certificates, PPSR search against Harbourglass, and confirmation of no options, convertibles, ESOP or other rights to shares.
  - Completion deliverables: original certificates (or a lost certificate indemnity), signed transfers, and a release of any security over the shares.

**2.3 Completion bonuses, AUD 420k plus on-costs (DD-005)**
- *Seller position:* a "matter for the Seller" and not shown in the funds flow.
- *Problem:* If the Company is the paying entity, the Buyer bears the cost after Completion. That is value leakage of at least AUD 420k. On-costs come on top and could add a material amount: NSW payroll tax, superannuation guarantee (verify whether the bonus is OTE), PAYG withholding and workers' compensation. The Seller's own disclosure leaves this point open.
- *Push for:*
  - All transaction bonuses and on-costs treated as **Transaction Costs/Debt**, deducted from the price.
  - Payment through payroll with correct withholding, funded by the Seller.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap and basket, for any bonus-related liability, including employee claims if the continued-employment conditions are disputed.
  - Clarity on who bears any bonus that vests after Completion.

**2.4 Bluefen consent, about 30% of FY26 revenue (cl 3/6.3)**
- *Seller position:* reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
- *Problem:*
  - "Reasonable endeavours" is too weak for a customer worth around AUD 3.6m in revenue.
  - Deeming the condition satisfied on delivery of *a* consent ignores the cl 11.3 conditions. The Seller admits there is no evidence those are satisfied.
  - A conditional or qualified consent could leave the contract terminable or re-priced.
- *Push for:*
  - A condition precedent satisfied only by an **unconditional** written consent, in a form reasonably acceptable to the Buyer, together with evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - The condition waivable by the Buyer only.
  - All reasonable endeavours (or best endeavours) by the Seller, with the Buyer given visibility over communications with Bluefen.
  - A long-stop date with a Buyer walk right.
  - If the Buyer waives the condition: a price adjustment or earn-out holdback, or a specific indemnity for loss of the contract within an agreed period.

### Tier 2: Specific known risks that need ring-fencing

**2.5 Ironquay IP (DD-004 cl 7.3; cl 11.1)**
- *Seller position:* the existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- *Problem:* The risk is title to the SOW3 Project Materials, not the AUD 180k invoice. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership transfers only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, and there is no receipt or assignment in the data room. If the materials are embedded in the Company's product, the exposure includes infringement claims, injunctions, licensing or re-development costs, and customer impact. Verify how core these materials are.
- *Push for:*
  - Payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees before or at Completion, at the Seller's cost or treated as Debt.
  - Completion deliverables: Ironquay's written confirmation of receipt, and a confirmatory deed of assignment (including moral rights consents where relevant) as a condition or completion deliverable.
  - Expanding the cl 11.1 indemnity to all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 materials. This should sit outside the general cap, basket and disclosure, with a separate cap and a longer claim period.

**2.6 DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)**
- *Seller position:* a "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- *Problem:*
  - About 1,240 records of personal information were sent via a link to an unintended external address. Business emails and names are still personal information.
  - With revenue of roughly AUD 12m, the Company is almost certainly an APP entity under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). The Notifiable Data Breaches scheme requires a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within 30 days of reasonable grounds to suspect an eligible data breach.
  - As at 22 September the assessment was "preliminary". It is now 6 November, so a compliance failure may already have occurred.
  - Penalty and enforcement exposure has increased following the 2024 Privacy Act amendments, and the statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy is in force.
  - Customer contracts (possibly including Bluefen) may contain their own notification obligations.
- *Push for:*
  - Immediate disclosure of current status: the date of awareness, the assessment outcome, whether the OAIC and individuals have been notified, whether the link was accessed (from server logs), and a forensic or incident report.
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and any required notifications, with Buyer consultation.
  - A **specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the incident, outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with a claim period of at least 3 years. This should cover regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation, remediation, notification costs and third-party claims.
  - Consider a retention or escrow amount.

**2.7 Sandbar renewals, AUD 330k (DD-008/DD-011)**
- *Seller position:* ordinary-course operating costs.
- *Problem:*
  - The Seller's own disclosure says the three renewals should be read together for timing and scope, and does not say they are ordinary course, terminable or accrued.
  - Three related renewals of AUD 110k each is a pattern consistent with splitting a commitment to stay under an approval or disclosure threshold. Verify the threshold in the conduct-of-business clause.
  - If Sandbar is a Seller-related party, this may be leakage.
- *Push for:*
  - Copies of all three agreements, their dates, terms, termination rights, and confirmation of any relationship between Sandbar and the Seller.
  - If entered during the conduct-of-business period without Buyer consent, treat as a breach.
  - If prepaid or committed outside ordinary course, treat as Debt or a price adjustment, or have the Seller procure termination at its cost.
  - A specific warranty that they are arm's length and on ordinary commercial terms.

**2.8 Tax**
- *Seller position:* "settled under the general regime".
- *Problem:* An 18-month limit is well short of ATO amendment periods.
- *Push for:*
  - A separate tax indemnity (or tax deed) covering pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and superannuation guarantee charge, which links to the bonuses.
  - A claim period of at least the relevant amendment period plus a buffer (commonly 5 to 7 years).
  - Cap at 100% of the price.
  - No general disclosure or knowledge bar against tax warranties.

### Tier 3: Limitation regime and drafting

**2.9 "All limitations apply to all Claims" (cl 12.3/13; 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- *Problem:* This sweeps in specific indemnities, title, tax, completion obligations, leakage, restraints, and arguably fraud. It would neutralise every point above.
- *Push for:* express carve-outs from all limitations for:
  - fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment or wilful misconduct by the Seller or its representatives (contracting out of liability for fraud is in any event ineffective);
  - Fundamental Warranties, tax and specific indemnities (each with its own cap and time limit);
  - completion, price, leakage and restraint covenants;
  - equitable relief, including injunctions and specific performance.

  The exclusive-remedy clause should apply only to general warranty claims.

**2.10 Non-reliance (cl 20.5)**
- Accept non-reliance on extra-contractual statements only. Make clear that the Buyer *does* rely on the Warranties and Disclosure Letter, and that nothing excludes liability for fraud. Note that non-reliance clauses carry evidentiary weight against misleading or deceptive conduct claims under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law. That is a reason to make the Warranties do the work.

**2.11 General disclosure (Sch 7; DL §1.1–1.2)**
- *Problem:* Disclosing the whole data room and public registers shifts all diligence risk to the Buyer.
- *Push for:*
  - Disclosure only of matters **fairly disclosed** with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, made against specific Warranties.
  - Data room disclosure, if conceded at all, limited to documents specifically referenced in the Disclosure Letter. The data room must be indexed and archived on a USB or electronic copy.
  - No general disclosure against Fundamental Warranties, tax, or the specific indemnities.
  - Accept DL §1.4 (non-admission) only if it is stated not to limit the Buyer's indemnity rights.

**2.12 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)**
- *Problem:* The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew or *could have discovered*. This is the most damaging clause in the package.
- *Push for:* deletion and replacement with a pro-sandbagging clause, so the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge. As a fallback, limit it to matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. Under no circumstances should it apply to indemnities, title or tax.

**2.13 Cap and thresholds (cl 12.1–12.2)**
- A 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) for general warranties is within market range. We can trade on it, possibly toward 25–30% or a W&I-backed structure, in exchange for the carve-outs above.
- The basket is proposed as a **deductible**. Push for a **tipping** basket so that, once AUD 250k (about 1%) is exceeded, the Buyer recovers from the first dollar.
- De minimis: seek AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated.
- The specific indemnities sit outside both thresholds.

**2.14 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- These are lower risk, but the Seller's phrasing ("does not describe…", "does not state…") is a careful non-conclusion, not comfort.
- *Lease:* make the landlord notification a Seller-procured completion deliverable.
- *Mossvale:* we should form our own view on whether the assignment restriction includes a deemed assignment or change-in-control limb. If there is doubt, seek a comfort letter or add a condition.

---

## 3. Protecting the price

Because W&I insurance will exclude known matters, consider a **retention or escrow** (for example, 10–15% of the price for 18–24 months, to be sized after diligence) to back the Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar and Bluefen-related indemnities. Separately, the debt-free/cash-free mechanics should deduct the following from the AUD 24m headline price: Riverlark payout (about AUD 3.2m or more), bonuses and on-costs (AUD 420k or more), outstanding Ironquay SOW3 fees (AUD 180k if unpaid pre-Completion), and any non-ordinary-course Sandbar commitments.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Release post-Completion | Repay from funds flow at Completion; payout letter, deed of release, PPSR discharge; treat as Debt | Critical |
| 2 | Title | Share register; general cap and 18 months | Fundamental Warranty, 100% cap, 6+ years; independent ASIC/PPSR verification | Critical |
| 3 | Bonuses AUD 420k + on-costs | Excluded from funds flow | Treat as Transaction Costs deducted from price; specific indemnity | Critical |
| 4 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfied on consent | Unconditional consent plus cl 11.3 evidence; Buyer-only waiver; long-stop; walk right | Critical |
| 5 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Pay pre-Completion; receipt and confirmatory assignment; full IP indemnity outside cap | High |
| 6 | DD-006 privacy incident | "Not expected to be material" | Immediate NDB status update; pre-Completion covenant; uncapped or separately capped specific indemnity; escrow | High |
| 7 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Full documents; related-party check; consent breach analysis; Debt/price adjustment or termination at Seller cost | High |
| 8 | Tax | General regime | Tax indemnity/deed; ATO amendment period plus buffer; 100% cap | High |
| 9 | Limitations apply to all Claims | Yes | Carve out fraud, Fundamental Warranties, tax, indemnities, covenants, equitable relief | High |
| 10 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Actual and constructive knowledge bar | Delete; pro-sandbagging | High |
| 11 | General disclosure | Whole data room and public records | Fair, specific disclosure only; none against fundamentals, tax or indemnities | High |
| 12 | Cap and basket | 20%; deductible basket AUD 250k; de minimis AUD 25k | Tipping basket; de minimis AUD 10–15k; cap as trading chip | Medium |
| 13 | Non-reliance | All Claims | Limit to extra-contractual statements; preserve reliance on Warranties; fraud carve-out | Medium |
| 14 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent required | Notice as completion deliverable; independent analysis of Mossvale; comfort letter if in doubt | Low–Medium |
| 15 | Stale disclosure | As at 22 Sept 2026 | Updated disclosure; bring-down at signing and Completion | Medium |

**Recommended next steps:**
1. Send the Seller an issues list built on Tier 1 and the limitation carve-outs, and refuse to negotiate the cap until those are agreed.
2. Request Riverlark payout figures, the Bluefen cl 11.3 status, Ironquay payment evidence, the DD-006 incident file and NDB status, and the Sandbar agreements immediately.
3. Have our privacy and IP specialists assess DD-006 and DD-004 so the indemnities and escrow can be sized.
4. Update the price model for the debt-like items above.

Please send me the full SPA draft and the DD reports, and I can convert this into a clause-by-clause mark-up.

- *Seller position:* a "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- *Problem:*
  - About 1,240 records of personal information were sent via a link to an unintended external address. Business emails and names are still personal information.
  - With revenue of roughly AUD 12m, the Company is almost certainly an APP entity under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). The Notifiable Data Breaches scheme requires a reasonable and expeditious assessment, generally within 30 days of reasonable grounds to suspect an eligible data breach.
  - As at 22 September the assessment was "preliminary". It is now 6 November, so a compliance failure may already have occurred.
  - Penalty and enforcement exposure has increased following the 2024 Privacy Act amendments, and the statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy is in force.
  - Customer contracts (possibly including Bluefen) may contain their own notification obligations.
- *Push for:*
  - Immediate disclosure of current status: the date of awareness, the assessment outcome, whether the OAIC and individuals have been notified, whether the link was accessed (from server logs), and a forensic or incident report.
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and any required notifications, with Buyer consultation.
  - A **specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the incident, outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with a claim period of at least 3 years. This should cover regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, investigation, remediation, notification costs and third-party claims.
  - Consider a retention or escrow amount.

**2.7 Sandbar renewals, AUD 330k (DD-008/DD-011)**
- *Seller position:* ordinary-course operating costs.
- *Problem:*
  - The Seller's own disclosure says the three renewals should be read together for timing and scope, and does not say they are ordinary course, terminable or accrued.
  - Three related renewals of AUD 110k each is a pattern consistent with splitting a commitment to stay under an approval or disclosure threshold. Verify the threshold in the conduct-of-business clause.
  - If Sandbar is a Seller-related party, this may be leakage.
- *Push for:*
  - Copies of all three agreements, their dates, terms, termination rights, and confirmation of any relationship between Sandbar and the Seller.
  - If entered during the conduct-of-business period without Buyer consent, treat as a breach.
  - If prepaid or committed outside ordinary course, treat as Debt or a price adjustment, or have the Seller procure termination at its cost.
  - A specific warranty that they are arm's length and on ordinary commercial terms.

**2.8 Tax**
- *Seller position:* "settled under the general regime".
- *Problem:* An 18-month limit is well short of ATO amendment periods.
- *Push for:*
  - A separate tax indemnity (or tax deed) covering pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and superannuation guarantee charge, which links to the bonuses.
  - A claim period of at least the relevant amendment period plus a buffer (commonly 5 to 7 years).
  - Cap at 100% of the price.
  - No general disclosure or knowledge bar against tax warranties.

### Tier 3: Limitation regime and drafting

**2.9 "All limitations apply to all Claims" (cl 12.3/13; 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- *Problem:* This sweeps in specific indemnities, title, tax, completion obligations, leakage, restraints, and arguably fraud. It would neutralise every point above.
- *Push for:* express carve-outs from all limitations for:
  - fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment or wilful misconduct by the Seller or its representatives (contracting out of liability for fraud is in any event ineffective);
  - Fundamental Warranties, tax and specific indemnities (each with its own cap and time limit);
  - completion, price, leakage and restraint covenants;
  - equitable relief, including injunctions and specific performance.

  The exclusive-remedy clause should apply only to general warranty claims.

**2.10 Non-reliance (cl 20.5)**
- Accept non-reliance on extra-contractual statements only. Make clear that the Buyer *does* rely on the Warranties and Disclosure Letter, and that nothing excludes liability for fraud. Note that non-reliance clauses carry evidentiary weight against misleading or deceptive conduct claims under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law. That is a reason to make the Warranties do the work.

**2.11 General disclosure (Sch 7; DL §1.1–1.2)**
- *Problem:* Disclosing the whole data room and public registers shifts all diligence risk to the Buyer.
- *Push for:*
  - Disclosure only of matters **fairly disclosed** with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, made against specific Warranties.
  - Data room disclosure, if conceded at all, limited to documents specifically referenced in the Disclosure Letter. The data room must be indexed and archived on a USB or electronic copy.
  - No general disclosure against Fundamental Warranties, tax, or the specific indemnities.
  - Accept DL §1.4 (non-admission) only if it is stated not to limit the Buyer's indemnity rights.

**2.12 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)**
- *Problem:* The clause bars claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew or *could have discovered*. This is the most damaging clause in the package.
- *Push for:* deletion and replacement with a pro-sandbagging clause, so the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge. As a fallback, limit it to matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. Under no circumstances should it apply to indemnities, title or tax.

**2.13 Cap and thresholds (cl 12.1–12.2)**
- A 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) for general warranties is within market range. We can trade on it, possibly toward 25–30% or a W&I-backed structure, in exchange for the carve-outs above.
- The basket is proposed as a **deductible**. Push for a **tipping** basket so that, once AUD 250k (about 1%) is exceeded, the Buyer recovers from the first dollar.
- De minimis: seek AUD 10–15k, with related claims aggregated.
- The specific indemnities sit outside both thresholds.

**2.14 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- These are lower risk, but the Seller's phrasing ("does not describe…", "does not state…") is a careful non-conclusion, not comfort.
- *Lease:* make the landlord notification a Seller-procured completion deliverable.
- *Mossvale:* we should form our own view on whether the assignment restriction includes a deemed assignment or change-in-control limb. If there is doubt, seek a comfort letter or add a condition.

## 3. Protecting the price

Because W&I insurance will exclude known matters, consider a **retention or escrow** (for example, 10–15% of the price for 18–24 months, to be sized after diligence) to back the Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar and Bluefen-related indemnities. Separately, the debt-free/cash-free mechanics should deduct the following from the AUD 24m headline price: Riverlark payout (about AUD 3.2m or more), bonuses and on-costs (AUD 420k or more), outstanding Ironquay SOW3 fees (AUD 180k if unpaid pre-Completion), and any non-ordinary-course Sandbar commitments.
